questions.q: Why does a reference-field column cost more to render in a list than a plain string or number column?
options: The table only stores a sys_id, so the platform must perform an additional lookup against the referenced table to resolve and display the actual value, for every row
Reference fields are always empty, so the platform skips rendering them
Reference fields are stored as images, which take longer to load
There is no real cost difference between any column types
questions.explain: A plain value is already in the row's data; a reference column requires resolving a sys_id into a human-readable value, repeated for every row shown.

questions.q: What's a strong hint that a list's default filter/sort condition lacks a matching index?
options: The list is slow on its default view but noticeably faster once a different filter is applied
The list loads instantly regardless of which filter is applied
The list has fewer than five columns
The list has no Related Lists on its form
questions.explain: If performance improves markedly under a different filter, the default condition likely lacks the index that would let the database retrieve matching rows quickly — full depth on indexing comes in Chapter 3.

questions.q: Why do many Related Lists on one form add up to real cumulative load cost?
options: Each Related List runs its own separate query against its own table when the form loads, independent of every other Related List
Related Lists share a single query, so adding more costs nothing extra
Related Lists only load when a user manually clicks a button
Only the very first Related List on a form ever actually queries data
questions.explain: The cost is cumulative because each Related List fires its own query on load — it's the sum of all of them together that matters, not just the single worst one.

questions.q: What's the right question to ask when reviewing a slow list's columns or a slow form's Related Lists?
options: Does this need to be shown here, by default, every time this loads — not just whether it could be shown
Could this theoretically be displayed somewhere on this record
Does the field have a long enough display name
Is this the newest field added to the table
questions.explain: Almost anything could be shown; the useful diagnostic question is whether it's genuinely necessary by default, every single load.

questions.q: A list view has six reference-field columns and its form has eight Related Lists. What do both problems have in common?
options: Each individually adds a small, reasonable cost, but the total across many of them accumulates into real, measurable slowness
Both problems are actually unrelated to performance and are purely cosmetic
Reference columns and Related Lists are the same underlying feature with different names
Removing either one has no measurable effect on load time
questions.explain: Both follow the same underlying pattern as UI-Policy overload from Lesson 2: individually cheap, cumulatively costly when left unreviewed.
